title: Railroad Time — The line that made time
dek: Say a railroad clue. Four sourced eras move the scene, the story, and the train.
body:
Railroad Time is a small history room built around four changes that moved more than trains: public steam on the Stockton & Darlington Railway in 1825; the Chinese labor behind the transcontinental railroad in 1869; North American railway time in 1883; and the Tokaido Shinkansen in 1964. Each stop has its own original scene and a direct source from Historic England, the National Park Service, the Smithsonian, or JR Central.

Speak or type a clue such as steam, workers, clocks, or bullet train. The room routes the words locally through a fixed set of historical keywords, moves to the matching stop, and can read the station card aloud with the browser's voice. The transcript stays editable. PointCast does not receive or store microphone audio or transcripts; the browser or device may use its own speech service. No live AI request chooses the history, and visited station IDs last for the browser session only.

The four pictures were made with OpenAI image generation. They are historical interpretations, not documentary photographs. The facts remain attached to named sources, and the generated pictures are labeled inside the room and its machine-readable companion.
